segmentation.text: When stopping is required
at a railroad crossing
the driver
shall keep as far to the right of the highway
as possible
and
shall not form two lanes of traffic
unless the highway is marked for four or more lanes of traffic.

elements.justification: "Stopping" (DEF-NRS-484A-260) is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle"; that it is required is read through the devices in the scene that require a halt of the subject's traffic: dev.railway_signal_or_gate, "the devices at a level crossing; lights in {flashing, dark}; gate in {up, lowering, down, raising, none}", with lights flashing or the gate lowering or down; dev.stop_sign, "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"; dev.traffic_signal showing circular_red; dev.human_direction with indication stop and role police_officer or railroad_flagger. Each must govern (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"). dev.governs is "not a stand-in for a position": the place of the stop is not read from governance but from s2's distance to the crossing. dev.traffic_signal is not a sign; the signal's state is read, not a sign's.

st.railway_crossing: "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail"; "railroad" (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is "a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails": a level crossing of a railway with the roadway is a railroad crossing, and a streetcar line laid along the street forms no level crossing of a railway with the roadway, so the definition's exclusion is already made by the contract. The subject is at the crossing where st.region_geometry, "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)", is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach; region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, and no occupancy is read from it.

"Driver" (DEF-NRS-484A-080) means "every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle": the duty binds the conduct of a vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"); ru.aggregate is not a stand-in for the relational role of who drives, which is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

The right of the highway the subject is on: st.highway "the entire public way between its boundary lines" occupied by the subject (rel.occupies); st.road_edge "curb or edge of the roadway" lying on that way (st.on_way, "the public way a structure region lies on"); the edge is on the subject's right where prim.region_lateral_offset, "the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user", is negative. st.on_way is not nearness to a way: the edge's belonging to the way is read from the relation, not from distance.

operationalizations.standard: as far to the right of the highway as possible
operationalizations.convention: A vehicle kept as far right as it can be placed stands with its body within the curb clearance of a parallel-parked car plus lane-keeping variability and an edge margin of the right-hand edge of the roadway: the ground distance from its body to a road edge on its right (st.region_geometry, prim.region_lateral_offset negative) is at most p.pullover_edge_gap. A vehicle in any lane but the rightmost, or wandering left within the rightmost, is farther.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle; its body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of a railroad crossing c (st.railway_crossing, st.region_geometry); and some device d governs (dev.governs) a travel region r whose footprint the subject overlaps (rel.occupies) and requires a halt of r's traffic at this observation: a dev.railway_signal_or_gate whose lights are flashing or whose gate is lowering or down, a dev.stop_sign, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer or railroad_flagger with indication stop.
obligation: At every such observation, some st.road_edge e lies on a highway h the subject occupies (st.on_way(e, h), rel.occupies(subject, h)), lies to the subject's right (prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, e) < 0), and the ground distance from the subject's body to e (st.region_geometry) is at most p.pullover_edge_gap. Where no such edge is found the duty is violated; where the offset or the distance of every candidate edge is unobserved, unknown.

narrowings.why: "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.
That a device is official, placed by a public authority or railroad, is read from its presence.
"the right of the highway" is read as the right-hand edge of the roadway; a shoulder beyond that edge is not a place the vehicle is required to move onto.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Railway signal lights flashing and gate down govern the two-lane approach of a one-way roadway; the subject car halts 8 m from the railway crossing in the left lane, its body 4.5 m from the right-hand road edge (prim.region_lateral_offset negative), farther than p.pullover_edge_gap.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane 10 m from a railway crossing on a two-lane two-way highway; the subject car halts straddling the centre line, its body 2.5 m from the right-hand road edge.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same crossing and flashing lights; the subject car halts 8 m from the crossing in the rightmost lane, its body 0.4 m from the right-hand road edge.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car is 8 m from a railway crossing whose lights are dark and gate up; no stop sign, red signal or stop direction governs its lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Lights flashing govern the subject's lane near a crossing; the source maps regions without their outline, so the distance to the crossing and to the road edge is unobserved.

param_proposals.name: p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a vehicle's body to a railroad grade crossing within which the vehicle is at the crossing, on the stretch where a halt for the crossing is made: the 50-ft outer bound of the zone in which grade-crossing practice places the halt before the nearest rail
param_proposals.source: MUTCD Part 8 highway-rail grade crossing stop-line placement and the Uniform Vehicle Code grade-crossing stop zone

param_proposals.name: p.pullover_edge_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between a vehicle body and the right-hand curb or roadway edge within which a vehicle pulled over to clear the way counts as as close to the edge as it can be placed: the curb clearance of a parallel-parked car (about 0.3 m) plus lane-keeping variability and an edge margin
param_proposals.source: parallel-parking curb clearance and lane-keeping variability in naturalistic driving data

segmentation.text: When stopping is required
at a railroad crossing
the driver
shall keep as far to the right of the highway
as possible
and
shall not form two lanes of traffic
unless the highway is marked for four or more lanes of traffic.

elements.justification: "Stopping" (DEF-NRS-484A-260) is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle"; that it is required is read through the devices in the scene that require a halt of the subject's traffic: dev.railway_signal_or_gate, "the devices at a level crossing; lights in {flashing, dark}; gate in {up, lowering, down, raising, none}", with lights flashing or the gate lowering or down; dev.stop_sign, "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"; dev.traffic_signal showing circular_red; dev.human_direction with indication stop and role police_officer or railroad_flagger. Each must govern (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"). dev.governs is "not a stand-in for a position": the place of the stop is not read from governance but from s2's distance to the crossing. dev.traffic_signal is not a sign; the signal's state is read, not a sign's.

st.railway_crossing: "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail"; "railroad" (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is "a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails": a level crossing of a railway with the roadway is a railroad crossing, and a streetcar line laid along the street forms no level crossing of a railway with the roadway, so the definition's exclusion is already made by the contract. The subject is at the crossing where st.region_geometry, "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)", is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach; region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, and no occupancy is read from it.

"Driver" (DEF-NRS-484A-080) means "every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle": the duty binds the conduct of a vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"); ru.aggregate is not a stand-in for the relational role of who drives, which is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

Two lanes of traffic are formed at the crossing where another member of "traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-285, "pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel", the admitted aggregate) stands or moves beside the subject in a lane (st.lane, "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles"; rel.occupies), so that two lines of traffic face the crossing side by side: rel.same_direction, "headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance", and rel.longitudinal_overlap positive, "the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)" — a projection, "neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies", and only side-by-side position is read from it. The other road user is at the same crossing c where its body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of c (st.region_geometry, claimed with s2). Requiring the other to occupy a lane leaves out a pedestrian on a sidewalk, which forms no lane of traffic.

The highway the subject occupies (st.highway, rel.occupies) is marked for four or more lanes where at least four distinct lanes (st.lane, "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles") lie on it (st.on_way, "the public way a structure region lies on"), counted over both directions; st.lane is not a half of the roadway, and the count is of lane regions, not of lateral positions. The literal four is the text's figure.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle; its body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of a railroad crossing c (st.railway_crossing, st.region_geometry); and some device d governs (dev.governs) a travel region r whose footprint the subject overlaps (rel.occupies) and requires a halt of r's traffic at this observation: a dev.railway_signal_or_gate whose lights are flashing or whose gate is lowering or down, a dev.stop_sign, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer or railroad_flagger with indication stop. Exception: the duty does not apply where the highway h the subject occupies has at least four pairwise distinct lanes lying on it (st.lane, st.on_way(l, h)).
obligation: At every such observation, no road user v other than the subject (not same(v, subject)), a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, occupying a lane (st.lane, rel.occupies), whose body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of the same crossing c, travels in the subject's direction (rel.same_direction with tolerance p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos) side by side with the subject (rel.longitudinal_overlap of subject and v positive). Where such a v exists the duty is violated; where none can exist it is complied with, also when the subject is alone.

narrowings.why: "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.
That a device is official is read from its presence.

Forming two lanes is read as the subject standing or moving side by side with another road user in a lane, both at the crossing; which of the two came alongside the other is not told apart, so both are held to have formed the second line.
"marked" lanes are read from the mapped lane regions: a represented lane is read as a marked one.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane two-way highway (two lanes on the way); railway lights flashing govern the subject's lane; another car halts 10 m from the crossing in the right lane, and the subject car pulls up beside it in the opposing lane, same direction, longitudinal overlap 3 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same two-lane highway and flashing lights; the subject car halts in the right lane 8 m behind the other car (longitudinal overlap negative); no road user beside it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Lights dark and gate up at the crossing, no stop sign, red signal or stop direction governs the subject's lane; two cars pass side by side.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Flashing lights govern the subject's lane on a two-lane highway; another car halts beside it at the crossing in the same direction, but the longitudinal overlap is unobserved.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Four-lane highway (four lanes lie on the way, two per direction); flashing lights; the subject car halts in the left same-direction lane beside a car in the right lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane highway, flashing lights; the subject car halts alone at the crossing, no other road user in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a vehicle's body to a railroad grade crossing within which the vehicle is at the crossing, on the stretch where a halt for the crossing is made: the 50-ft outer bound of the zone in which grade-crossing practice places the halt before the nearest rail
param_proposals.source: MUTCD Part 8 highway-rail grade crossing stop-line placement and the Uniform Vehicle Code grade-crossing stop zone

param_proposals.name: p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two road users standing or moving side by side count as travelling the same way: the heading spread of vehicles queued in adjacent lanes
param_proposals.source: lane-change and queue heading variability in naturalistic driving data

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:
When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,
to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping
due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing; or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.

As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.

elements.justification: "vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"; "driver" (DEF-NRS-484A-080, "every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle") is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion, not membership.

Crossing at grade the track of a railroad: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.railway_crossing, "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail". "Railroad" (DEF-NRS-484A-200) excludes streetcars; a streetcar line along a street forms no level crossing of a railway with the roadway, so the contract makes that exclusion. The crossing is under way from the observation the footprint overlaps the crossing until the subject has completely crossed (a5).

"without stopping": drv.motion.complete_halt, "The road user is at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets" (p.halt_speed_tolerance). Failing to completely cross without stopping is a halt at an observation of the crossing before the subject has completely crossed. The concept says nothing of where the road user is; the place is read from a2 and a5.

The causes the words name (no room beyond the crossing, the undercarriage hanging on the crossing) are why a vehicle comes to rest on the tracks; they are read through the conduct they explain, the halt before completely crossing (drv.motion.complete_halt), as the ontology reads a purpose by its conduct.

"the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail": st.region_geometry, "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)", from the subject's body to the st.railway_crossing whose outline carries "its nearest rail". While the subject has been within the literal 15 ft of the crossing at every observation since its footprint last overlapped it, its trailing end is not yet 15 ft past the rail; region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, which a2 reads with rel.occupies.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle crossing a railroad crossing c and not yet completely across it: at this observation the ground distance from its body to c (st.region_geometry) is below the literal 15 ft, and has been below it at every observation since an observation (this one included) at which its footprint overlapped c (rel.occupies) — the past `since` of 'distance below 15 ft' over 'occupies c'.
obligation: At every such observation the subject is not halted: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold. A halt while it overlaps c, or after leaving c with its trailing end less than 15 ft past c, is a violation.

narrowings.why: "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.

The causes of the halt (insufficient space beyond the crossing, insufficient undercarriage clearance) are not observed; they are read through the halt before completely crossing they explain, so any halt in that stretch is judged.

"completely cross", as the definition in this section states it, is read with the nearest rail as the outline of the mapped crossing region and the trailing end as the subject's body outline: the distance from body to crossing outline stands for the distance from the trailing end to the nearest rail.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject truck enters the railway crossing (rel.occupies), the queue ahead stops it, and it comes to rest (kin.speed 0) with its body 2 m past the crossing outline, below 15 ft.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car traverses the crossing without halting and halts in the queue with its body 8 m past the crossing outline.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car never overlaps a railway crossing; it halts at an intersection far from any track.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car is on the crossing (rel.occupies true) but the source does not supply kin.speed, so whether it halts is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car comes to rest while its footprint still overlaps the crossing.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of vehicle tracking sources

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:
To fail to obey an official traffic-control device or the directions of a police officer
at a railroad crossing.

elements.justification: "vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"; "driver" (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"Official traffic-control device" (DEF-NRS-484A-145) is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic"; at a railroad crossing its members that direct the subject's entry are dev.railway_signal_or_gate ("the devices at a level crossing; lights in {flashing, dark}; gate in {up, lowering, down, raising, none}": obeyed by not entering while the lights flash or the gate is not up), dev.traffic_signal (circular_red: not entering), dev.stop_sign ("regulatory sign requiring a full halt": a halt, drv.motion.complete_halt, on the approach short of the crossing, within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach by st.region_geometry) and dev.yield_sign ("requiring yielding without a mandatory halt": not entering while a rail vehicle, ru.rail_vehicle, closes within the conflict horizon — prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, which are "not a stand-in for contact" and are read only as the conflict bound). "Police officer" (DEF-NRS-484A-180, "every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic") is dev.human_direction of role police_officer; its indication stop is obeyed by not entering. Each device must govern (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies) at its entry; dev.governs is not a position, and the place of the halt is read from the distance to the crossing.

The device or direction is obeyed at a railroad crossing: the event judged is the subject's entry into a st.railway_crossing, "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail", the observation at which its footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies) having not overlapped it at the previous one. "Railroad" (DEF-NRS-484A-200) excludes streetcars, which form no level crossing of a railway with the roadway.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle and enters a railroad crossing c at this observation: rises(rel.occupies(subject, c)) for some st.railway_crossing c.
obligation: At the entry observation, for every device d that governs (dev.governs) a travel region r the subject occupies at that observation: (i) d a dev.railway_signal_or_gate: its lights are not flashing and its gate is not lowering, down or raising; (ii) d a dev.traffic_signal: it does not display circular_red; (iii) d a dev.human_direction of role police_officer: its indication is not stop; (iv) d a dev.yield_sign: no rail vehicle q (ru.rail_vehicle) has prim.closest_approach_within(subject, q) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance at most p.conflict_centre_clearance; (v) d a dev.stop_sign: the subject halted before this entry. For (v) the search runs back from the entry: a halt counts at an observation where drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) holds with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, the subject's footprint does not overlap c, and its body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of c (st.region_geometry). The search ends at the last observation before the entry at which the subject's body was farther from c than p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach (the approach start: only an observed exit from that zone begins a new approach), or at the previous entry of the subject into c. Finding the halt meets the duty; reaching either end without it violates it; where the recording begins with the subject already within the reach of c and no halt is observed since, or the distance to c is unobserved at an observation the search reads and no halt is found, the duty is unknown. Where no device governs a region the subject occupies at the entry, the duty is complied with.

narrowings.why: "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.
That a device is official, placed by a public authority or railroad, is read from its presence.

Obedience is read at the subject's entry into the crossing, through the devices and directions that govern that entry (railway lights and gate, a red signal, a stop or yield sign, a police officer's stop); instructions that do not bear on entering the crossing, and a direction to proceed, are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Railway signal lights flashing, gate down, governing the subject's approach lane; the subject car drives around the gate and its footprint comes to overlap the railway crossing.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Railway signal lights dark, gate up, governing the subject's lane; the subject car enters the crossing.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives along a street with no railway crossing; it never overlaps one.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car enters a crossing; a railway signal with lights flashing stands at the crossing but the source does not observe which regions it governs.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane at the crossing; the subject car approaches from 60 m, halts 6 m from the crossing (kin.speed 0), then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane; the subject approaches from 60 m and enters the crossing at 8 m/s without halting.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A police officer (dev.human_direction role police_officer, indication stop) governs the subject's lane; the subject enters the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: The subject enters an unsignalled crossing with no device governing its lane; no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane; the recording begins with the subject 10 m from the crossing moving at 3 m/s, no halt is observed, and it enters the crossing.
scenarios.boundary: the subject's approach to the crossing from beyond p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach, which lies before the recording's first observation

param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are erected giving notice thereof,
a person shall not drive a vehicle
onto or from any controlled-access highway
except at those entrances and exits which are indicated by such devices.

elements.justification: "Official traffic-control device" (DEF-NRS-484A-145) is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority"; the devices giving notice of where a controlled-access highway may be entered and left are dev.regulatory_sign, "a point regulation by catalogue code", with code entrance or exit; their erection is read from the presence of such a sign in the scene. A sign is "not a stand-in for a manoeuvre or a road feature": the sign is read, not the ramp.

"vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"; "a person ... drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"Controlled-access highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-060) is "every highway to or from which ... persons have no legal right of access except at such points only": st.controlled_access, "a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes". Driving onto it is the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies, which lists the controlled-access lane among its regions) having not overlapped it at the previous one; driving from it is the observation at which it ceases to overlap it, having overlapped it at the previous one.

An entrance or exit indicated by such devices is a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... a lane, ... roadway, ... shoulder") by a dev.regulatory_sign of code entrance (for driving onto) or exit (for driving from). The subject drives onto the highway at an indicated entrance where, at its entry, it occupies (rel.occupies) such an entrance-governed region; it drives from it at an indicated exit where, at the last observation it overlapped the highway, it occupied such an exit-governed region. dev.governs is never a controlled-access region itself, so the governed lane is read, and "not a stand-in for a position" is respected: no halt place is read from it.

applicability: Some dev.regulatory_sign with code entrance or exit is present in the scene; the subject is a vehicle; and at this observation it enters a controlled-access highway ca (rises(rel.occupies(subject, ca))) or leaves it (rises(not rel.occupies(subject, ca))).
obligation: At an entry into ca: the subject occupies some travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code entrance. At a departure from ca: at the previous observation the subject both occupied ca and occupied some travel region r governed by a dev.regulatory_sign of code exit; written as rises(not X) where X is 'occupies ca and occupies a region governed by an exit-coded regulatory sign', which at a departure (X false here) holds exactly when X held at the previous observation. Otherwise the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: "a person ... drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.
That entrance and exit signs are official and give notice of the controlled access is read from their presence in the scene.
An entrance or exit indicated by the devices is read as a travel region an entrance- or exit-coded regulatory sign governs.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Entrance- and exit-coded regulatory signs govern the ramps; the subject car leaves a frontage road, crosses the verge, and its footprint comes to overlap the controlled-access region in a mainline lane no entrance sign governs.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car enters the controlled-access region through a ramp lane governed by an entrance-coded regulatory sign.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car stays on a surface street; its footprint never overlaps a controlled-access region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Entrance signs are present and the subject car enters the controlled-access region, but the source does not observe which regions the signs govern.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car leaves the controlled-access region; at the previous observation it occupied an exit lane governed by an exit-coded regulatory sign.

scenarios.name: branch_2

segmentation.text: Except if required by an emergency
or as otherwise authorized by subsection 3
[(3) appended below],
a person shall not drive a vehicle
on a controlled-access highway:
Upon any portion of the highway that lies outside of a marked traffic lane or marked entrance or exit lane.
A person driving a vehicle described in
paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210
[list appended below]
may drive that vehicle on a paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.
The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to:
(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480;
(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490;
(c) A traffic incident management vehicle;
(d) A tow car;
(e) A coroner vehicle;
or (f) A public transit motor bus,
that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

elements.justification: An emergency requiring the movement is not observable; it is read through the conduct that shows it: the subject's hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard, "both indicators flashing together", as a disabled or imperilled vehicle shows), or the subject an emergency vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle, "vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency") showing a lit warning lamp (sig.warning_lamp, "a warning lamp lit"). ru.emergency_vehicle is "not a stand-in for a responding emergency vehicle — the class alone is not responding": the class is read only together with its lit warning lamp, and an unobserved lamp leaves the exception unknown.

Authorization by subsection 3 is the permission subsection 3 states (spans e7, e10, e12-e18): a shoulder-use permission posted by a dev.regulatory_sign, "a point regulation by catalogue code", of code shoulder_use_permitted; this span joins that permission to the duty as an exception.

"vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway". "drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle is moving, drv.motion.complete_halt ("at rest at the observation ... speed at or below a tolerance the caller sets") not holding with p.halt_speed_tolerance.

"Controlled-access highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-060, "every highway to or from which ... persons have no legal right of access except at such points only"): st.controlled_access, "a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes", whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, which lists the controlled-access lane).

A portion of the highway outside a marked traffic lane or entrance or exit lane: a st.shoulder ("the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic") or a st.median_or_divider ("physical barrier or dividing section between roadways") whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or no st.lane ("a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles") overlapped at all while the subject is on the controlled-access highway. Lanes include the entrance and exit lanes of st.controlled_access. st.lane is not a lateral position within a lane: membership is read from occupancy.
The person driving a vehicle of the classes listed (e12-e17): the subject vehicle, admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; which vehicles are described is read from the list.

On a paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.shoulder whose paved attribute holds while it occupies the st.controlled_access region. Lawfully placed signage allowing that vehicle to use the shoulder: a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governing that shoulder (dev.governs lists the shoulder among the regions a device governs), whose structured conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold, "the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user", the class condition included). A sign is not a road feature: the permission is the sign's, read as it is posted.

"Authorized emergency vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, "a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law"; the words borrowed through the reference e8 list it as "(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480;". The citation of NRS 484A.480 describes that class and adds no condition the aggregate does not carry. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490;": a vehicle operating as an authorized emergency vehicle under permit is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, "a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws"; the permit is the legal basis of that membership, which the run's reading classifies. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(c) A traffic incident management vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment", kind incident_management; it is "not a stand-in for an emergency vehicle", and none is read from it. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(d) A tow car;": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car, "a motor vehicle which has been altered or designed and equipped for and exclusively used in the business of towing vehicles". The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(e) A coroner vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment", kind coroner; not an emergency vehicle. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"or (f) A public transit motor bus,": a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus ("a vehicle ... designed and used for the transportation of persons for compensation") that is ru.transit_bus, "bus in public transit service, identifiable by its livery or route display"; the aggregate is not replaced by the class atom, the class atom states the public-transit qualification the words add. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

Being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway: the listed vehicle occupies (rel.occupies) a paved st.shoulder lying on (st.on_way) the st.highway it is on; where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder: a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governs (dev.governs) that shoulder and its conditions hold for the vehicle (prim.conditions_hold). st.on_way is not nearness: the shoulder belongs to the way by the relation. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

compositions.quote: (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;
compositions.why: The reference borrows only the list of vehicle classes NRS 484B.210(4) sets forth (an authorized emergency vehicle, one under permit as such, a traffic incident management vehicle, a tow car, a coroner vehicle, a public transit motor bus) to name which vehicles subsection 3 permits on a signed paved shoulder; no rule of NRS 484B.210 (its passing on the right, or its exemption from it) needs to apply, hold or be complied with for this duty or its exception, and the list's words are appended in this line and carried by its own elements.

residues.why: Introduces the list of NRS 484B.210(4) as appended; the exemption from the passing rule of NRS 484B.210(1)(c)(1) it states is that section's, not this duty's, and is not read here.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle in motion (drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) with p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold) whose footprint overlaps a controlled-access highway ca (rel.occupies, st.controlled_access). Exception (emergency): the duty does not apply where the subject's hazard lamps flash (sig.hazard) or the subject is an emergency vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle) with a lit warning lamp (sig.warning_lamp).
obligation: The subject's footprint overlaps no st.median_or_divider; overlaps no st.shoulder other than an authorized one; and overlaps some st.lane unless every non-lane region it overlaps is an authorized shoulder. A shoulder s is authorized (subsection 3) where the subject is a listed vehicle — a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, a ru.official_vehicle of kind incident_management or coroner, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car, or a member of DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus that is ru.transit_bus — and s is paved, lies on the highway the subject is on (st.on_way, st.highway), and is governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold).

narrowings.why: "a person shall not drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle in motion is driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
An emergency is read through the conduct that shows it: hazard lamps flashing, or an emergency vehicle showing a lit warning lamp.

"marked" lanes are read from the mapped lane regions; the portions outside them are read as shoulders, medians and dividers, and any footprint position on the controlled-access highway that overlaps no lane.
"lawfully placed" signage is read from the presence of a shoulder_use_permitted sign governing the shoulder.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character
at:
A rate of speed greater than
that posted by a public authority
for the particular portion of highway being traversed.

elements.justification: "drive or operate" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: kin.speed, "magnitude of velocity", the motion the duty judges; the same words map to kin.speed in the run's index.

"a vehicle of any kind or character": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", whatever its class.
The rate of speed is kin.speed, "magnitude of velocity" (m/s), compared strictly greater than the posted value.

The speed posted: dev.speed_limit_sign, "sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit", of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone, read as the value dev_speed_limit_sign_value (m/s). "Public authority" (DEF-NRS-484A-195, "the Department of Transportation or the local authority having jurisdiction") is the sign's legal source, read from the sign's presence.

The particular portion of highway being traversed is the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) that the sign governs (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"). dev.governs is "not a stand-in for a position": no halt place is read from it, only which portion the posting covers.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone.
obligation: For every such sign d governing a travel region the subject occupies, kin.speed(subject) is not greater than dev_speed_limit_sign_value(d).

narrowings.why: "drive or operate" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
That the speed is posted by a public authority is read from the presence of the speed limit sign.
